open_points.subject: Syncthing conflict copy model
open_points.text: The deliverer does not offer such a copy.
open_points.question: Is a Syncthing conflict copy a Photo entity with a conflict/ineligible status, a separate ConflictCopy model, or an unmanaged filesystem artifact from which no runtime model is minted?
options: Photo entity with a conflict/ineligible status
No runtime model; excluded filesystem artifact
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an excluded filesystem artifact and mint no Photo until it is renamed.

witness.initial: A normal photo file exists and has a Syncthing conflict copy beside it.
outcomes: The deliverer reads a Photo entity whose status prevents offering.
The deliverer creates no model for the conflict copy.
witness.observer: The owner and any component querying stored photo records

open_points.subject: Photo identity across rename
open_points.text: the owner who wants that version renames it, after which it is an ordinary photo.
open_points.question: Does renaming preserve the conflict copy's identity while changing its status, or does it end the conflict-copy identity and create a new ordinary Photo identity?
options: Preserve one entity identity and change its status
Create a new Photo identity and retire or discard the conflict-copy identity
No identity exists before rename; mint the first identity afterward
open_points.default_guess: No product identity exists before rename; mint a new Photo identity when the renamed file is discovered.

witness.initial: A conflict copy is present but has not been offered.
events: The owner renames the conflict copy.
The deliverer next reads the folder.
outcomes: The same entity becomes an ordinary photo.
A newly minted Photo represents the renamed file.
witness.observer: The owner viewing history and any consumer holding photo identifiers

open_points.subject: Ordinary Photo minting authority and evidence
open_points.text: after which it is an ordinary photo.
open_points.question: Who mints the ordinary Photo identity after the rename, and from what stable evidence is that identity derived?
options: The owner action conceptually mints it from the renamed file
The deliverer mints it when discovering the renamed path
The Portal mints it when the file is delivered
The photo content or hash determines identity
open_points.default_guess: The deliverer mints the Photo from its discovery of the renamed filesystem entry, using a generated identifier independent of the path and content.

witness.initial: A conflict copy is renamed while the deliverer is not running.
events: The deliverer starts and discovers it.
The deliverer sends it to the Portal.
outcomes: The Photo identity exists from the owner's rename or filesystem identity.
The Photo identity is minted only by the deliverer or Portal.

open_points.subject: Conflict-copy lineage
open_points.text: Syncthing keeps the other version as a conflict copy beside it.
open_points.question: Must the model record that the conflict copy and the ordinary file are versions of the same logical photo, or are they unrelated candidate files once observed?
options: Both versions reference one logical Photo identity
Each file is a distinct Photo with an explicit lineage relation
They are independent and no lineage fact is modeled
The conflict copy is not modeled, so no relationship exists
open_points.default_guess: Do not model the conflict copy or a lineage relationship; after rename, treat the file as an independent Photo candidate.

witness.initial: One device's version has already been delivered and the other version exists as a conflict copy.
events: The owner renames the conflict copy.
The deliverer discovers the renamed file.
outcomes: The renamed file is another version of the already known logical photo.
The renamed file is a distinct ordinary photo with no modeled relation to the prior delivery.
witness.observer: The owner reviewing duplicates and delivery history

open_points.subject: Offer eligibility after rename
open_points.text: The deliverer does not offer such a copy. The file stays in the folder, and the owner who wants that version renames it, after which it is an ordinary photo.
open_points.question: Does the rename transition make the file eligible for a new offer, merely remove the conflict-copy exclusion while leaving other eligibility facts unchanged, or update an existing photo without creating another offer?
options: Rename makes it a new offerable Photo
Rename only removes the conflict exclusion; ordinary eligibility rules still decide
Rename updates the existing logical Photo and does not create a new offer
open_points.default_guess: Rename only removes the conflict-copy exclusion; the resulting Photo then follows the same eligibility lifecycle as any other ordinary photo.

witness.initial: The original version has already been delivered hidden, and its conflict copy remains beside it.
events: The owner renames the conflict copy.
The deliverer performs its next delivery flow.
outcomes: The renamed version is offered as a new hidden photo.
The renamed version updates or is suppressed as the already delivered logical photo.
witness.observer: The owner reviewing delivered photos in the Portal
